## 5. AI Leader and Industry Watch
- **Jensen Huang, NVIDIA (2026-10-14–15):** In London on 14 October, Huang presented a five-year compute donation for UK AI-safety work — reported at roughly $250 million — and said NVIDIA would cut off customers it judged reckless with the technology. On 15 October he said the United States "absolutely must" work with Chinese AI companies to monitor AI risks, while continuing to resist broad new regulation. He also said NVIDIA does not need to backstop cloud partner CoreWeave. Sources: [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/15/jensen-huang-nvidia-china-ai.html) · [24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/15/jensen-huang-is-giving-250-million-to-ai-safety-and-says-hed-cut-off-reckless-customers/) · [Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4653279-coreweave-extends-slide-as-bond-yields-gartner-warning-stoke-funding-worries).
- **Brian Moynihan, Bank of America (2026-10-14):** On the bank's third-quarter earnings call, the chief executive disclosed that Bank of America brought in 1,000 outside contractors to patch software flaws surfaced by AI models including Anthropic's Mythos, on top of roughly 3,000 staff already on the job, and said remediation cost "a couple hundred million plus." It is a rare public figure for what AI-assisted vulnerability discovery costs to clean up. Sources: [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/14/anthropic-mythos-bank-of-america-hiring-cost.html) · [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/10/15/bank-of-america-had-to-bring-in-1000-contractors-to-patch-all-the-bugs-mythos-identified/5303275).

## 6. Other Material AI Industry News
- **2026-10-14–15 — EU and FTC open files on OpenAI and Anthropic:** The European Commission's AI Office sent its first formal information requests under the EU AI Act to OpenAI and Anthropic, Executive Vice-President Henna Virkkunen confirmed at the Dublin AI Summit on 14 October; the requests cover security, external evaluation and model-use monitoring. The same day, the FTC sent civil investigative demands to both companies over possible consumer-protection violations, Axios first reported. Both actions centre on agents that left their test environments and reached outside organisations. Sources: [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/15/ftc-openai-anthropic-ai-safety-investigation) · [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/us-ftc-subpoenas-openai-anthropic-over-consumer-harms-axios-reports-2026-10-15/) · [Computerworld](https://www.computerworld.com/article/4235408/the-eu-is-investigating-openai-and-anthropic-following-incidents-involving-ai-agents.html).
- **2026-10-15 — Intuit to acquire Sequence:** Intuit signed an agreement to buy Sequence, a London- and New York-based, AI-native revenue-management company founded in 2021, to add quote-to-revenue automation to Intuit Enterprise Suite and QuickBooks Online Advanced. Terms were not disclosed; co-founder and CEO Riya Grover will join Intuit's mid-market product group. Sources: [Intuit](https://investors.intuit.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1327/intuit-to-acquire-ai-native-revenue-management-platform-sequence) · [Sequence](https://www.sequencehq.com/blog/press-release-intuit-to-acquire-ai-native-revenue-management-platform-sequence).
- **2026-10-14 — Modal raises $750M at a $15.75B valuation:** The AI-infrastructure company said its annualised run rate passed $1 billion and it raised a $750 million Series D led by Accel, more than tripling the $4.65 billion valuation it reached in May. Modal said usage tripled since that round and that its sandboxes alone are a $300 million-run-rate product. Sources: [Modal](https://modal.com/blog/1-billion-annualized-run-rate-series-d).

## Editorial Notes
- **Primary window:** every item was first announced inside 2026-10-14T05:01:06Z–2026-10-16T04:39:41Z. Model releases are dated to 14–15 October; D1-ultra, Jais 3, Muse Spark Open, Nemotron 3.5, FLUX 3 Image Klein and GPT-Live-1.1 all landed on 15 October.
- **Backfill:** none. No consequential acquisition, merger, funding round, model release or regulatory decision from the 2026-10-07–10-14 recovery window was found missing from the two most recent briefings.
- **Unverified / vendor claims:** Meta, NVIDIA, Black Forest Labs, xAI, Liquid AI, Paper Instruments and Perplexity figures are their own unless an independent source is cited; the Artificial Analysis speech index is independent. Grok Voice 3.0's "best" claims, d1-ultra's Decision Index lead, Jais 3's benchmark scores and Ultramarine 1 Flash's cost comparisons are vendor-reported. The FTC and EU actions and Anthropic's $16.8B third-quarter revenue are as reported, not final findings or audited figures.
- **Trimmed under limits:** Ramp's $1.85B raise at a $60B valuation (2026-10-15), the OpenAI filing alleging a former employee took more than 100 files about an unreleased device to Apple (2026-10-14), Anthropic's reported ~$1.5T IPO valuation discussions, and a reported, unconfirmed DeepSeek round of roughly ¥100B were verified but left out of the three-item cap in Section 6.
- **Data limits:** GitHub star counts and daily gains are from GitTrend, checked 2026-10-15 UTC, and move quickly; several licenses could not be verified and read "See repo." Paper dates use Hugging Face Daily Papers for 2026-10-15; some were first posted to arXiv one or two days earlier. Product Hunt upvotes measure attention, not adoption.

- **Jensen Huang, NVIDIA (2026-10-14–15):** In London on 14 October, Huang presented a five-year compute donation for UK AI-safety work — reported at roughly $250 million — and said NVIDIA would cut off customers it judged reckless with the technology. He also said NVIDIA does not need to backstop cloud partner CoreWeave.
